# Coffee Bean Origin Classifier

> Send one photo of whole coffee beans, green or roasted, and get back the country the coffee was most likely grown
> in, with a score for every country the model knows, or a refusal when the photo does not look like the beans it
> was trained on. Free, no key, no account. The photo is never stored.

The service is one HTTP endpoint, `POST /analyze`, behind the web page. It is meant for people with a phone, and is
open to agents acting for a person (send their photo, report the answer) and to scripts on other sites' pages.

## API

- [OpenAPI description](https://coffee.kasetkin.com/openapi.json): the request, both answer parts and every error,
  machine-readable.
- [Agent resource manifest](https://coffee.kasetkin.com/.well-known/ard.json): this file and the API, for agent
  registries.

Call it with one multipart form upload:

```
curl -sS -F photo=@beans.jpg https://coffee.kasetkin.com/analyze
```

- `photo` (required): the image file. JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC/HEIF, AVIF, JPEG XL, GIF, BMP and camera RAW (DNG, CR2,
  CR3, NEF, ARW, RAF, ORF, RW2, PEF, SRW); any other format is refused. A RAW file needs its usual extension in the
  filename. An animated GIF is read as its first frame. At most 40 MB and 60 megapixels (a RAW file: 16 megapixels).
- `skip_crop` (optional): send `1` to classify the whole photo instead of the beans the server finds in it.

The answer is `application/x-ndjson`: two JSON objects, one per line, streamed.

1. `{"part": "preview", ...}` after about 2 s: the photo as the model sees it (`thumbnail`, a base64 JPEG), the bean
   region (`mask`, a base64 PNG or null), the crop (`box`, fractions of the photo as `[x0, y0, x1, y1]`, or null).
   An agent can skip this line.
2. The result, after about 9 s in all. `{"part": "classification", "verdict": ...}`, where `verdict` is one of:
   - `predicted`: `ranked` lists every country as `{"id", "label", "score"}`, best first; `label` is the country.
   - `warned`: the same `ranked`, plus `warning` ("Uncertain", "Uncertain framing"): say the answer is unsure.
   - `refused_ood`: the photo does not look like coffee beans the model knows. There is no country to report.
   - `refused_unreadable`: the photo could not be read as beans.

   Or `{"part": "error", "message": ...}` if the server failed after the preview went out.

Errors before the stream starts, each with `{"error": ...}`: `400` (no photo, or a file that is not an image), `413`
(a photo over 40 MB, or over its megapixel limit), and `503`, which is one of two:

- `{"error": "the classifier is busy with another photo"}`, or a `503` without a JSON body: another photo is being
  analyzed. Wait about 10 s and retry.
- `{"error": "the classifier is offline"}`: the classifier is down or being updated. Try again in a few minutes; do
  not retry in a loop.

## From a web page

A script on a page of any site may call `POST /analyze` and read the answer: every answer, errors included, carries
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and exposes `X-Request-Id`, and a preflight is answered. Send no credentials; the API
takes none. The answer streams, so read it line by line:

```
const form = new FormData();
form.append("photo", file);   // a File, from an <input type="file"> for example
const response = await fetch("https://coffee.kasetkin.com/analyze", {method: "POST", body: form});
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`${response.status}`);   // 400, 413 or 503: see the errors above
const reader = response.body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader();
let text = "";
for (let chunk = await reader.read(); !chunk.done; chunk = await reader.read()) {
  text += chunk.value;
  for (let end; (end = text.indexOf("\n")) >= 0; text = text.slice(end + 1)) {
    const part = JSON.parse(text.slice(0, end));   // "preview", then "classification" or "error"
    console.log(part.part, part.verdict);
  }
}
```

A site that calls the API from its page:

- should tell its visitors that their photo is sent to this service, which never stores it;
- shares the one worker with this page and every other caller: on a busy `503`, wait about 10 s and retry once,
  never in a loop and never in parallel, as in Limits below;
- can quote the answer's `X-Request-Id` when it reports a problem.

## Limits

- One photo at a time for everyone: the server has one worker. On a busy `503`, wait about 10 s and retry; do not
  send photos in parallel.
- At most 40 MB and 60 megapixels a photo, and 16 megapixels for a camera RAW file: the server converts each photo
  within a fixed memory budget. A phone photo is under both; a camera's full-size RAW may not be, so send a smaller
  export or a JPEG.
- Use a photo of a handful of whole beans filling most of the frame. Ground coffee, other seeds or a photo with no
  beans is refused, by design.
- About 10 countries, scored against each other; a coffee from anywhere else still gets the closest of them.

## Background

- [What the model knows](https://github.com/kasetkin/coffee-vision#what-it-knows): the countries, and which have
  green and roasted photos.
- [How it works](https://github.com/kasetkin/coffee-vision#how-it-works): segmentation, a frozen DINOv3 model with
  a linear head, and the out-of-distribution guard.
- [Source code](https://github.com/kasetkin/coffee-vision): the public repository.
- [Web page](https://coffee.kasetkin.com/): the same service for a person with a phone.
